chunks: “The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم commanded us regarding sacrificial animals that we inspect the eye and the ear, and he forbade us from the torn-eared, the split-eared, the one cut from the front, and the one cut from the back.”

key_terms.الشَّرْقَاءِ: an animal with an ear split lengthwise
key_terms.الْأَضَاحِيِّ: sacrificial animals offered at the time of sacrifice
key_terms.الْأُذُنَ: the ear of the sacrificial animal, whose condition is examined
key_terms.الْخَرْقَاءِ: an animal with a torn or perforated ear
key_terms.الْعَيْنَ: the eye of the sacrificial animal, whose soundness is checked
key_terms.الْمُدَابَرَةِ: an animal whose ear is cut from the back
key_terms.الْمُقَابَلَةِ: an animal whose ear is cut from the front
key_terms.نَسْتَشْرِفَ: to inspect carefully and examine attentively

ai.seo_question: What defects in the ears or eyes make a sacrificial animal unsuitable in hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal instruction concerning sacrificial animals, requiring attention to the soundness of their eyes and ears. It shows that outward defects in the animal are relevant in the fiqh of sacrificial offerings and that this ruling is rooted in the sunnah of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم as transmitted by Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3047 - Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) said:

"The Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace and blessings be upon him and his family) commanded us regarding sacrifices that we examine the eyes and ears of the animal and avoid one that is defective in the ears, such as being torn, slit, cut from the front, or cut from the back."
